finds.title: PM statement on Iran: 1 March 2026
finds.author: Prime Minister Keir Starmer
finds.evidence_quote: The United States has requested permission to use British bases for that specific and limited defensive purpose.
finds.line: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Britain accepted a US request to use British bases for a specific and limited defensive purpose against Iran.
finds.about: This is the Prime Minister's published statement on Iran, issued on 1 March 2026. Starmer said Iran was striking British interests and that Gulf partners had asked Britain to do more. He said the US had asked to use British bases and that Britain accepted, while not joining the strikes.
finds.ties_to: UK-US basing arrangements; bases used to launch attacks on Iran
finds.because: This permission opened British bases such as RAF Fairford to US operations against Iran, which led Iran to name those bases as targets and later made them the focus of security threats.

finds.title: Jimmy Carter
finds.author: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum
finds.source: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library and Museum (National Archives)
finds.evidence_quote: When his father died in 1953, he resigned his naval commission and returned with his family to Georgia.
finds.line: Carter resigned his Navy commission after his father died in 1953 and returned to Georgia to take over the Carter farms.
finds.about: This is the biography page kept by Carter's own presidential library. It gives his birth in Plains, his Navy years and his return home in 1953. It says he took over the family farms and ran a seed and farm supply company with his wife.
finds.ties_to: came back in 1953 after the Navy to run the family business
finds.because: Running the farm tied Carter to this land for the rest of his life, which is why the family still held it when he died.

finds.title: Public Law 100-206: An Act to establish the Jimmy Carter National Historic Site and Preservation District in the State of Georgia, and for other purposes
finds.author: 100th Congress of the United States
finds.source: U.S. Government Publishing Office (govinfo), Statutes at Large
finds.evidence_quote: To establish the Jimmy Carter National Historic Site and Preservation District in the State of Georgia, and for other purposes.
finds.line: Public Law 100-206 became law on December 23, 1987, and established the Jimmy Carter National Historic Site and Preservation District in the State of Georgia.
finds.about: This law created the Jimmy Carter National Historic Site and Preservation District in the State of Georgia. It also covers other purposes beyond the site itself. The act was signed into law on December 23, 1987.
finds.ties_to: Jimmy Carter National Historical Park, run by the National Park Service
finds.because: This act put the federal government in charge of the Carter buildings in Plains, leaving the family farmland to be handled separately.

finds.title: Articles of Impeachment Against Donald John Trump (H.Res.755)
finds.author: U.S. House of Representatives, 116th Congress
finds.evidence_quote: Resolved, That Donald John Trump, President of the United States, is impeached for high crimes and misdemeanors and that the following articles of impeachment be exhibited to the United States Senate
finds.line: The House impeached President Trump on December 18, 2019, in a resolution that sent articles of impeachment to the Senate.
finds.about: This is the enrolled text of House Resolution 755. It impeaches the President and lays out two articles, abuse of power and obstruction of Congress. The House passed it on December 18, 2019, and the Senate later voted not guilty on both articles.
finds.ties_to: a perfect phone call, impeachment vote in the House
finds.relation: earlier instance of the same action
finds.because: It showed that the House can impeach on a party-line vote while the Senate holds the power to convict, the same split Massie's articles now face.

finds.title: Kelly v. Hegseth, Memorandum Opinion (Document 37)
finds.author: Judge Richard J. Leon, U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia
finds.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, via Justia
finds.evidence_quote: As such, his motion for a preliminary injunction on his First Amendment claim is hereby GRANTED.
finds.line: Judge Richard Leon granted Sen. Mark Kelly a preliminary injunction on his First Amendment claim against Defense Secretary Hegseth.
finds.about: This is the district court's memorandum opinion in Kelly's suit over the Pentagon's censure and retirement grade proceeding. Judge Leon signed it on February 12, 2026. He held that Kelly was likely to win on the merits and granted the injunction.
finds.ties_to: the effort to punish Sen. Mark Kelly over a video reminding troops they can refuse illegal orders
finds.because: The ruling put the Kelly dispute before a court and made it one of the charges Massie later put into his articles of impeachment.

finds.title: The Constitution of the United States: A Transcription
finds.author: Constitutional Convention delegates
finds.evidence_quote: The President, Vice President and all civil Officers of the United States, shall be removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors.
finds.line: The Constitution of 1787 says the President, Vice President and all civil Officers can be removed from office for treason, bribery, or other high crimes.
finds.about: This transcription presents the Constitution of the United States as written in 1787. It includes a rule on removal from office. The President, Vice President and all civil Officers can be removed on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors.
finds.ties_to: eight articles of impeachment against the defense secretary
finds.because: The clause gave the House a way to charge a Cabinet officer, but it left open what counts as a high crime, so later fights over war powers went through Congress.

finds.title: Letter from GSA Administrator Emily W. Murphy to Joseph R. Biden, Jr.
finds.author: Emily W. Murphy, Administrator, U.S. General Services Administration
finds.evidence_quote: I take this role seriously and, because of recent developments involving legal challenges and certifications of election results, am transmitting this letter today to make those resources and services available to you.
finds.line: The head of the General Services Administration told Biden in a letter that federal transition resources and services were now available to him.
finds.about: Emily Murphy ran the General Services Administration, the agency that releases transition support under the Presidential Transition Act. Her letter to Biden is dated November 23, 2020. She says legal challenges and certifications of election results led her to make the resources available.
finds.ties_to: months of attacks on Biden and an effort to overturn the election results
finds.relation: earlier instance of the same action
finds.because: The formal handoff began only after weeks of delay, and the first presidential-level step toward Biden's inauguration was still ahead.

finds.title: President Biden Archived on X: "Today I met with President-elect Trump in the Oval Office."
finds.author: President Joe Biden
finds.evidence_quote: I look forward to leading a smooth transition and peaceful transfer of power.
finds.line: Biden said he met President-elect Trump in the Oval Office and promised a smooth transition and peaceful transfer of power.
finds.about: This is a post from Biden's archived presidential account, time-stamped November 13, 2024. It reports the Oval Office meeting with Trump and says Biden's team would do what it could to help the incoming administration. A photo shows Biden, Trump, Jeff Zients and Susie Wiles.
finds.ties_to: the two men met in the Oval Office after Trump's 2024 victory
finds.because: This meeting is the one Biden later describes in his book, where he says Trump was friendly in private.

finds.title: Biden says "what the hell's going on here?" about Trump's Greenland, Canada comments
finds.author: CBS News
finds.evidence_quote: In response to Biden's comments, White House spokesman Steven Cheung posted on social media that Biden is a "complete disgrace to this country and the office he occupied."
finds.line: White House spokesman Steven Cheung answered Biden's BBC interview by calling him a "complete disgrace to this country and the office he occupied."
finds.about: CBS News reported on Biden's BBC interview, his first since leaving office. The report says Cheung responded on social media to what Biden said about Trump. It records Cheung's words in the days after the interview.
finds.ties_to: a White House statement calling Biden "a disgrace"
finds.relation: earlier instance of the same action
finds.because: Cheung used nearly the same word for Biden months before the letter came out, so the later statement fit a pattern.
finds.why_no_primary: The statement was a social media post by a spokesman, and no archived copy from an agency or the White House was found, so a report written at the time carries it.

finds.title: Letter to the Honorable Howard Lutnick, Secretary, Department of Commerce
finds.author: Sen. Tom Cotton
finds.source: Office of Senator Tom Cotton, U.S. Senate
finds.evidence_quote: I write to you concerned about yet another case of diversion of American advanced chips to China through a network of shell companies and subsidiaries.
finds.line: Sen. Tom Cotton wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asking the department to investigate Megaspeed over the possible diversion of American chips to China.
finds.about: This is a letter dated October 13, 2025, from a Republican senator to the Commerce Secretary. It cites a news report on Megaspeed, describes it as a spin-off of a Chinese government-owned cloud company, and asks Commerce to look into its ownership and ties to U.S. chip companies.
finds.ties_to: Megaspeed, the company that would soon buy billions of dollars of Nvidia chips
finds.because: The letter put Megaspeed's chip purchases before the Commerce Department, whose inquiry later passed to the Justice Department and drew in Nvidia.

finds.title: NVIDIA CORP - Form 8-K (Item 8.01 Other Events, dated April 15, 2025)
finds.author: NVIDIA Corporation
finds.evidence_quote: The USG indicated that the license requirement addresses the risk that the covered products may be used in, or diverted to, a supercomputer in China.
finds.line: On April 15, 2025, NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K saying the U.S. government now requires a license for certain covered products.
finds.about: The filing falls under Item 8.01, Other Events. According to NVIDIA, the government indicated the license requirement addresses a risk. That risk is that the covered products may be used in, or sent to, a supercomputer in China.
finds.ties_to: Washington had barred Chinese buyers from those chips
finds.because: With China-bound sales blocked by license, the question of how Chinese firms still reached Nvidia chips drew attention to cloud customers such as Megaspeed.

finds.title: Nvidia Board to Probe Spying Case After CEO Jensen Huang Admits Infidelity
finds.author: Bloomberg News
finds.evidence_quote: Nvidia shares slid 4.3% on Monday, erasing nearly $200 billion in market valuation, after Huang disclosed the romantic relationship Sunday in a memo to employees.
finds.line: Nvidia shares slid 4.3% on Monday after Jensen Huang disclosed a romantic relationship to employees in a memo sent on Sunday.
finds.about: The slide erased nearly $200 billion in market valuation, according to the report. Huang made the disclosure in a memo to employees. The title says the Nvidia board will look into a spying case after the CEO admitted infidelity.
finds.ties_to: Huang told employees in a memo; stock closed down 4.3%; independent committee
finds.because: The memo and the share drop set off the board's committee and the shareholder suit that followed.
finds.why_no_primary: The memo and the market move are on record only in contemporary reporting; the memo is not posted in an archive and the stock close is not held in a public filing yet.

vetoed.title: Public Law 96-487: Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act
vetoed.author: 96th Congress of the United States; signed by President Jimmy Carter
vetoed.source: National Park Service (official copy of the public law)
vetoed.evidence_quote: To provide for the designation and conservation of certain public lands in the State of Alaska, including the designation of units of the National Park, National Wildlife Refuge, National Forest, National Wild and Scenic Rivers, and National Wilderness Preservation Systems, and for other purposes.
vetoed.line: Congress passed the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act, which Carter signed in December 1980, creating new park, refuge, river and wilderness units in Alaska.
vetoed.about: This is the text of Public Law 96-487, dated December 2, 1980. It sets up conservation units in Alaska across the National Park, Wildlife Refuge, Wild and Scenic Rivers, Wilderness and National Forest systems. The Conservation Fund points to it as the president's land legacy.
vetoed.ties_to: signed the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act in late 1980
vetoed.because: Carter's record as a president who protected public land is the line the Conservation Fund draws to the farm's later protection.
vetoed.vetoed_because: a number is not in the quote

vetoed.title: Georgia Forest Conservation Supports Gopher Tortoise Habitat
vetoed.author: The Conservation Fund
vetoed.evidence_quote: 4,361 acres in Webster County, protected with an NRCS conservation easement and managed as the new Lanahassee Creek WMA.
vetoed.line: The Conservation Fund and partners bought 4,361 acres in Webster County, Georgia, protected by an easement and managed as the new Lanahassee Creek Wildlife Management Area.
vetoed.about: This is a release from the same nonprofit that bought the Carter farm in 2026. It describes two Georgia forest purchases made to protect longleaf pine and gopher tortoise habitat. One of them became the new Lanahassee Creek WMA, the area the Carter land will join.
vetoed.because: That 2019 area is the neighbor the Carter farm will be added to, growing it to nearly 7,000 acres.

vetoed.title: Public Law 93-148, Joint Resolution Concerning the war powers of Congress and the President (War Powers Resolution)
vetoed.author: 93rd Congress of the United States
vetoed.source: U.S. Government Publishing Office, Statutes at Large
vetoed.evidence_quote: This joint resolution may be cited as the "War Powers Resolution".
vetoed.line: Congress enacted the War Powers Resolution on November 7, 1973, a joint resolution concerning the war powers of Congress and the President.
vetoed.about: This is the official Statutes at Large page for Public Law 93-148. Congress passed it as a joint resolution on war powers shared by Congress and the President. It is the law that sets rules for sending U.S. forces into hostilities without a declaration of war.
vetoed.ties_to: the Iran war, the boat strikes, the Maduro capture, the Yemen campaign
vetoed.because: The law set the legal test that critics now apply to military operations ordered without a new vote from Congress.

vetoed.author: Donald J. Trump
vetoed.evidence_quote: To all of those who have asked, I will not be going to the Inauguration on January 20th.
vetoed.line: Trump announced in a post on X that he would not attend Biden's swearing-in on January 20.
vetoed.about: This is Trump's own post from his @realDonaldTrump account, time-stamped January 8, 2021. It is a single sentence. It answers people who had asked whether the outgoing president would attend the inauguration of his successor.
vetoed.because: Twelve days later Trump stayed away from the ceremony and left a letter in the Oval Office instead.

vetoed.title: Implementation of Additional Export Controls: Certain Advanced Computing and Semiconductor Manufacturing Items; Supercomputer and Semiconductor End Use; Entity List Modification
vetoed.author: Bureau of Industry and Security, U.S. Department of Commerce
vetoed.evidence_quote: With this rule, BIS imposes new export controls on certain advanced computing semiconductor chips and computer commodities that contain such chips.
vetoed.line: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security imposed new export controls on certain advanced computing chips aimed at China.
vetoed.about: This is an interim final rule from the Commerce Department's export control bureau, released October 7, 2022 and printed in the Federal Register on October 13. It changed the Export Administration Regulations to add controls on advanced computing chips and on certain chip manufacturing items.
vetoed.ties_to: Washington had barred Chinese buyers from those chips
vetoed.because: This rule set the ban on advanced chip sales to China that later made routing chips through a third country a matter for investigators.
